Restructuring Plan: Two-Module Architecture

Source: RESTRUCTURING_PLAN.md

Executive Summary

Objective: Restructure sampleSizeCalc package into two distinct modules while maintaining backward compatibility and adding new study designs.

Current State: Monolithic 896-line file with 17 study designs in single switch statement.

Target State: Modular architecture with clear separation between diagnostic studies and drug trials, plus expanded design coverage.

I. Architecture Design

A. Module Structure (Single Package, Two Modules)

Decision: Keep as single R package with two logical modules, NOT two separate packages.

Rationale: - Simpler for users (single installation) - Shared S3 methods and validation functions - Shared dependencies (cli, rlang, stats) - Easier to maintain - Backward compatibility easier to ensure

II. Module 1: Diagnostic Studies

A. Current Designs (7)

  1. diagnosticAccuracySingle - Single diagnostic test accuracy
  2. diagnosticSuperioritySingle - Diagnostic superiority (single)
  3. diagnosticComparisonTwo - Two diagnostic measures comparison
  4. likelihoodRatioTest - Likelihood ratio estimation
  5. auc_single - Single AUC CI precision
  6. aucSuperiority - AUC superiority (single)
  7. aucComparison - AUC comparison (two tests)

B. New Designs to Add (4+)

  1. crossSectionalDiagnostic - Cross-sectional diagnostic studies
    • Method: Buderer (1996) precision-based formula
    • Parameters: sensitivity, specificity, prevalence, precision
    • Reference: Buderer NM (1996). Acad Emerg Med 3(9):895-900
  2. cohortDiagnostic - Cohort diagnostic studies (prospective/retrospective)
    • Method: Prevalence-adjusted formula
    • Parameters: sensitivity, specificity, prevalence, follow-up time
    • Reference: Song & Chung (2010), Akoglu (2022)
  3. rocComparisonMultiple - Multiple ROC curve comparison (multiple readers)
    • Method: Obuchowski-McClish for MRMC (Multi-Reader Multi-Case)
    • Parameters: AUC values, number of readers, correlation
    • Reference: Obuchowski NA (1998). Stat Methods Med Res 7(4):359-382
  4. observerAgreement - Observer agreement studies (kappa)
    • Method: Kappa coefficient sample size
    • Parameters: expected kappa, number of raters, number of categories
    • Reference: Sim & Wright (2005)

C. Design Type Parameter Prefix

All diagnostic designs will use prefix "diagnostic_": - diagnostic_accuracy_single - diagnostic_superiority_single - diagnostic_cross_sectional - diagnostic_cohort - diagnostic_roc_mrmc - diagnostic_observer_agreement

III. Module 2: Drug Trials

A. Current Designs (9)

  1. twoMeans - Two independent sample means
  2. twoProportions - Two independent proportions
  3. pairedMeans - Paired sample means
  4. survival - Survival analysis (log-rank)
  5. nonInferiorityMeans - Non-inferiority test (means)
  6. superiorityMeans - Superiority test (means)
  7. equivalenceMeans - Equivalence test (means)
  8. superiorityProportions - Superiority test (proportions)
  9. equivalenceProportions - Equivalence test (proportions)

B. New Designs to Add (7+)

  1. phaseIDoseEscalation - Phase I dose escalation (3+3 design)
    • Method: 3+3 design algorithm
    • Parameters: DLT rate, number of dose levels, target DLT rate
    • Reference: Oncology statistical methods
  2. phaseIISingleArm - Phase II single-arm (Simon’s two-stage)
    • Method: Simon’s optimal two-stage design
    • Parameters: p0 (unacceptable), p1 (acceptable), alpha, beta
    • Reference: Simon R (1989). Control Clin Trials 10(1):1-10
  3. groupSequential - Group sequential design
    • Method: O’Brien-Fleming or Pocock boundaries
    • Parameters: number of interim analyses, spending function
    • Reference: Jennison & Turnbull (2000)
  4. bioequivalence - Average bioequivalence (ABE)
    • Method: Two one-sided tests (TOST)
    • Parameters: CV, theta0 (ratio), design (2x2 crossover)
    • Reference: FDA guidance, Chow & Liu (2009)
  5. doseResponse - Dose-response studies (MCP-Mod)
    • Method: Multiple Comparison Procedure - Modeling
    • Parameters: dose levels, model type (Emax, sigEmax, etc.)
    • Reference: Bretz et al. (2005). Biometrics 61:919-929
  6. multiArmTrial - Multi-arm trials
    • Method: Dunnett’s test or Bonferroni correction
    • Parameters: number of arms, adjustment method
    • Reference: Dunnett (1955)
  7. adaptiveDesign - Adaptive design with sample size re-estimation
    • Method: Conditional power approach
    • Parameters: interim look, conditional power threshold
    • Reference: Wassmer & Brannath (2025)
  8. clusterRandomized - Cluster randomized trials
    • Method: ICC-adjusted sample size
    • Parameters: cluster size, ICC, number of clusters
    • Reference: Donner & Klar (2000)

C. Design Type Parameter Prefix

All drug trial designs will use prefix "drug_": - drug_two_means - drug_two_proportions - drug_survival - drug_phase_i_dose_escalation - drug_phase_ii_single_arm - drug_group_sequential - drug_bioequivalence - drug_dose_response - drug_multi_arm - drug_adaptive - drug_cluster_randomized

IV. Backward Compatibility Strategy

A. Keep Original Function

Maintain: sample_size_calculator() with original 17 design names

Implementation: Wrapper function that: - Accepts original design names (e.g., “twoMeans”, “diagnosticAccuracySingle”) - Internally routes to new modular functions - Returns same S3 object structure - No breaking changes for existing users

B. Add New Main Functions

Provide: Two new main functions for module-specific access:

# Module 1: Diagnostic studies
diagnostic_sample_size(
  design = c("accuracy_single", "superiority_single", "comparison_two",
             "likelihood_ratio", "auc_single", "auc_superiority",
             "auc_comparison", "cross_sectional", "cohort",
             "roc_mrmc", "observer_agreement"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  ...
)

# Module 2: Drug trials
drug_trial_sample_size(
  design = c("two_means", "two_proportions", "paired_means",
             "survival", "non_inferiority_means", "superiority_means",
             "equivalence_means", "superiority_proportions",
             "equivalence_proportions", "phase_i", "phase_ii",
             "group_sequential", "bioequivalence", "dose_response",
             "multi_arm", "adaptive", "cluster_randomized"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  ...
)

C. Deprecation Path

Original function: Never remove, but add deprecation notice for old design names

Timeline: - Version 3.0: Introduce new functions, keep old working - Version 4.0: Add deprecation warnings for old design names - Version 5.0: Old design names still work but documented as deprecated

V. Implementation Order

Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1)

  1. Create new file structure (directories, empty files)
  2. Extract validation functions to utils/
  3. Extract S3 methods to s3_methods/
  4. Create module entry points (diagnostic_sample_size, drug_trial_sample_size)

Phase 2: Refactor Existing Code (Week 2)

  1. Move current diagnostic designs to diagnostic/ files
  2. Move current drug trial designs to drug_trials/ files
  3. Update main sample_size_calculator() to call modular functions
  4. Test backward compatibility

Phase 3: Add Diagnostic Designs (Week 3)

  1. Implement crossSectionalDiagnostic
  2. Implement cohortDiagnostic
  3. Implement rocComparisonMultiple (basic version)
  4. Implement observerAgreement
  5. Update documentation

Phase 4: Add Drug Trial Designs (Week 4)

  1. Implement phaseIDoseEscalation (3+3 design)
  2. Implement phaseIISingleArm (Simon’s two-stage)
  3. Implement bioequivalence (TOST)
  4. Implement basic doseResponse (single model)
  5. Update documentation

Phase 5: Testing & Validation (Week 5)

  1. Test all existing designs still work
  2. Test new designs with known examples
  3. Run R CMD check
  4. Update vignettes with new designs
  5. Update README

Phase 6: Advanced Features (Future)

  1. Complete rocComparisonMultiple (full MRMC)
  2. Complete doseResponse (MCP-Mod with multiple models)
  3. Implement groupSequential (basic version)
  4. Implement adaptiveDesign (basic version)
  5. Implement multiArmTrial
  6. Implement clusterRandomized

VI. Testing Strategy

A. Unit Tests

For each design: - Test parameter validation - Test calculation against known values (from literature) - Test edge cases (boundary values) - Test error conditions

B. Integration Tests

Backward compatibility: - Test all 17 original designs produce identical results - Test S3 methods work with all designs - Test plot methods work

C. Validation Tests

Cross-validation: - Compare results with other R packages (TrialSize, PowerTOST, pROC, epiR) - Compare with manual calculations from published examples - Compare with online calculators

VII. Documentation Updates

A. Man Pages

Create/update: - sample_size_calculator.Rd - Add note about new functions - diagnostic_sample_size.Rd - New - drug_trial_sample_size.Rd - New - Individual design function .Rd files (auto-generated from roxygen2)

B. Vignettes

Update sampleSizeCalc.Rmd: - Add section on two-module architecture - Add examples of new diagnostic designs - Add examples of new drug trial designs - Include comparison tables

C. README

Update README.md: - Add section on module organization - Add quick examples for each module - Update feature count (17 → 30+) - Add reference to new functions

D. Formula Documentation

Update docs/FORMULA_SUMMARY.md and docs/formula_reference_guide.md: - Add formulas for new designs - Add references for new designs - Organize by module

VIII. Dependencies

Current Dependencies (Keep)

  • cli - Parameter validation error messages
  • rlang - Argument matching
  • stats - Core statistical functions (qnorm, power.t.test, power.prop.test)

Optional Dependencies (Keep)

  • ggplot2 - Plot method (Suggests)
  • scales - Plot formatting (Suggests)

New Dependencies to Consider

  • None initially - Implement basic versions first
  • Future: Consider specialized packages for advanced designs (DoseFinding, rpact, gsDesign) as Suggests

X. Success Criteria

Minimum Viable Release (MVR)

Full Release Target

XI. Risk Mitigation

Risk 1: Breaking Existing Code

Mitigation: Comprehensive backward compatibility tests, never remove original function

Risk 2: Incorrect Formulas

Mitigation: Validate all new designs against published examples and other R packages

Risk 3: Scope Creep

Mitigation: Implement basic versions first, advanced features in future releases

Risk 4: Documentation Overwhelm

Mitigation: Incremental documentation updates, use roxygen2 extensively
